analysis: Examined both head excerpts of docs/architecture/components/console-ui.md. No base excerpt or patch is supplied, so changed claims cannot be distinguished reliably from existing documentation. Lines 283–304 describe a replacement landing Next.js server with same-origin inference/usage, network, catalog/pricing and webhook routes, server-held credentials, and unavailable/fallback behavior. Integration must inspect landing/src/app/api/chat/route.ts for caller authorization, request/resource limits, shared-credential billing exposure (A-009), prompt/usage disclosure (A-001), and shared-account cache implications (T-041); inspect provider-stories/route.ts for submission limits and webhook destination/credential handling. These implementations and deployment configuration are absent, so documentation alone does not support a vulnerability finding. Console documentation describes fixed upstream resolution and credential forwarding (lines 89–127, 148–155), fail-closed sealing with trusted coordinator hop-by-hop decryption (180, 233–234), and trust metadata display (179); integration should verify any corresponding implementation changes against TB-002, T-008, T-052, T-053 and T-056. Analytics/privacy claims (194, 206–208, 236) require comparison with base and implementation before attributing new data exposure. No visible provider attestation, key custody, native runtime, cache crypto or fan-helper implementation changes are supplied. The compact canonical index and selected T-041 definition were considered; missing implementation/full boundary details limit conclusions.
